Design choice. About 10 requests a week per 1,000 active adults, so prayer screens stay busy in every dataset. The measured volume would need more requesters than active adults at the measured requests per requester (decision 67).
Design choice. Rock sets an expiration date whenever a request is approved, and the prayer team approves every request it keeps (decision 67).
Design choice. Long requests are built from a request and its details, and past about 500 characters they read as repetition (decision 67).
Design choice. The prayer team approves nearly every request, and a few wait in the approval queue (decision 67).
Design choice. The prayer team prays through requests (decision 67).
Design choice. A few requests are shared with a small group, so group prayer screens have data (decision 67).
Design choice. Every request carries the requester's campus, so campus filters have data (decision 67).
Design choice. The prayer team flags a few requests (decision 67).
Design choice. A prayer administrator approves almost every request by hand (decision 67).
Design choice. The prayer team approves requests the same day (decision 67).
Design choice. Weekend requests wait until a weekday (decision 67).
Design choice. The share of requests by how many times the team prayed for them. The average is about 6 (decision 67).
Design choice. Matches the prayer count mix (decision 67).
Design choice. Matches the prayer count mix (decision 67).
Design choice. An answer is a short note from the requester, as written in content/prayer (decision 67).
Design choice. Prayer team members ask for prayer too. A team of 3% of active adults can be at most about 4.5% of everyone who asks at this volume (decision 67).
Design choice. An active prayer team prays through requests in Rock (decision 67). Prayers per year follow from request volume times prayers per request, so they are not set here.
Design choice. The prayer team leaves short encouragements, as written in content/prayer, and a few requesters reply (decision 67).

Design choice. Notes show what good use looks like, not the thin use most churches have today, so who gets notes, how many, and how often features are used are set above the measured rates (decision 78). The measured shape is kept for timing, authors, and who notes are about.
Design choice. Good notes say a little more than the measured ones (decision 78).

The measured shape, with the overnight band cut to almost nothing. Overnight notes in the source come from time zone and import quirks, and staff write notes during the day.

notes: The sample church has a midweek student service, so a share of check-ins happen on Wednesday.
Christmas week shows almost no kids check-in, because many churches hold Christmas Eve services without children's ministry.
Dollar amounts (annual totals, gift sizes) should be reviewed as sources are added.

Prayer volume and its monthly pattern come from source-1. Categories, text length, timing, and who asks come from source-2. The prayer team's activity is a design choice, not a measurement (decision 67).

Person notes take their timing, authors, and who notes are about from source-3. Who gets notes, how many, and how often features are used are a design choice set above the measured rates (decision 78).
